summary: The verb describes the loss of courage under pressure and the harm done by discouraging others. The adjective in one reading of Psalm 10 describes the victims of the oppressor.

senses.definition: The persecutor pursues the needy and the brokenhearted. In Daniel the king loses heart when the ships of Kittim come against him.
Ezekiel accuses the prophets of disheartening the righteous by falsehood while strengthening the hands of the wicked.
The traditional two-word reading of Psalm 10:10 ends with this plural adjective. The surrounding lines describe people overcome by the strength of an attacker.

note: Psalm 10:10 has a single written form חלכאים and the traditional two-word reading חֵיל כָּאִים. Only the latter establishes a separate adjective here. Its syntax is uncertain. The Arabic cross-reference in Lane at p. 2582 supplies no independent definition adequate to settle the Hebrew sense.
